transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Do you have anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for reaching out. Yes, I do have some questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. So gardening is fine as part of light exercise.

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise, as well as lifting heavy objects, for about a month after your operation.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that advice. I appreciate it. I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them after surgery, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you can go ahead and use it as you were before. If you're running out and need more, your GP should be able to provide some for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to know, thanks! Another thing I wanted to ask is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
That's a common concern. It's actually quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain when it's bright, or severe light sensitivity — especially if your eye is also red and painful — that's not normal and we may need to assess this further. In that case, please let us know.

Is the light sensitivity mild, or are you experiencing pain or redness as well?
transcript.delivered: That's a common concern. It's actually quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, but also, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details about how long ago you had your surgery. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that covers everything I was wondering about. Thanks so much for your help, Dora!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm before we finish - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thank you for your support!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and best wishes with your recovery!
